english.title: Possess a flick knife or gravity knife
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) possessed a knife which had a blade that

(A)_[opened automatically from the closed position to the fully opened position, or from a partially opened position to the fully opened position by manual pressure applied to a button, spring or other device in or attached to the knife]_
(B)_[was released from the handle or sheath thereof by the force of gravity or the application of centrifugal force and which when released, was locked in place by means of a button, spring, lever, or other device]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 1(1A) and (1B)(a) of the Restriction of Offensive Weapons Act 1959.

english.notes:
(i) Definition of flick knife amended pursuant to Offensive Weapons Act 2019.
(ii) Defences are available at section 1(3) and 1(4).
(iii) Further offences available at H20295.
(iv) If a blade can be released by using gravity or centrifugal force, such as being held upside down or by a quick twist of the wrist, then it is a gravity knife. It is possible that a 'butterfly knife', if it had a locking device, could come within this definition, but such a case is yet to go before the courts.

6 monthsNote
In relation to an offence committed before section 281(5) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 comes into force, the reference to 51 weeks imprisonment in relation to summary offences is to be read as a reference to 6 months imprisonment.
